text: An OpenSSL pull request fixes "Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()" (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8) by returning -1 for invalid inputs: NULL input or output buffers, negative lengths, and lengths for which the encoded size does not fit in an int. The OpenSSL SRT has asked for it to be fixed publicly; the advisory is still pending. The author also suggests a similar guard for EVP_DecodeBlock().
evidence: OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)

text: PostgreSQL 19 has been released, with release notes published on postgresql.org. A Databricks post says PostgreSQL 19 is available on Lakebase the same day the community released it. A Snowflake engineering post describes a new REPACK and REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) feature for reclaiming bloated table space online without downtime, external extensions or table locks.

text: GamesIndustry.biz reports that the European Commission's publication of its draft Digital Fairness Act last week prompted uproar within the games industry. It says practices the act targets, such as loot boxes and pay-to-win, are wildly successful economically but not uniformly popular among players. The outlet's analysis argues the act hits European indies particularly hard.
evidence: How the EU's Digital Fairness Act will impact game design, and why it hits European indies particularly hard

The European Commission's publication of its draft Digital Fairness Act (DFA) last week prompted uproar within the games industry, with many notable voices candidly expressing their concerns. Opinions in the wider industry were more measured, possibly because some of the practices targeted by the DFA – such as loot boxes or pay-to-win – are wildly successful economically, but not uniformly popular amongst players.
